jobs.description:
Job Description

Ensite Services LLC — Contract (1099)

Ensite partners with solar and roofing companies nationwide to deliver fast, accurate residential site surveys. You visit homes, collect photos and measurements through our mobile app, and move on — no sales, no installs, just fieldwork you control.

Can start as early as this week, if you have all the required tools!

What you'll earn

$80 - $125 per survey completed

Surveys typically take 1–2 hours

Paid weekly, direct deposit

Same Day Pay available (On Request Basis)

What you'll do

Photograph the property and capture key measurements

Upload data through the Ensite app

Represent Ensite professionally with the homeowner

Safely access rooftops on 1–2 story homes

What you need (must have before applying)

25 ft+ extension ladder (your own)

Drone with Metadata Capabilities

Basic hand tools

Smartphone

Valid driver's license and reliable vehicle

Comfortable working at heights on rooftops

Background in solar, roofing, HVAC, home inspection, or construction

How it works

Set your availability in the app

Get notified when jobs open near you

Accept what you want, skip what you don't

Complete the survey — get paid that week

Join the nation's #1 residential site survey network. Company Description

Ensite Services LLC is a nationwide field services company supporting the residential solar and roofing industries through fast, accurate site survey solutions. We partner with leading solar and roofing providers across the country to help streamline pre-installation operations and deliver a smooth customer experience.

Our network of independent field technicians completes residential property assessments using mobile technology, photography, measurements, and drone imaging when needed. We focus on reliability, communication, and operational excellence — giving our clients the data they need to move projects forward efficiently.

jobs.title: Land Use and Environmental Attorney
jobs.description:
JOB TITLE:
Land Use & Environmental Attorney
FIRM:
Barbas Cremer, PLLC
LOCATION:
Tampa, FL (In-Person), 33606
FIRM SIZE:
<10 Employees
Job Type:
Full Time; Book of business not required

POSITION OVERVIEW

Barbas Cremer, PLLC is seeking a skilled and proactive Land Use and Environmental attorney to join our team in Tampa. We value "non-traditional" paths and are looking for a collaborative, ego-free professional with relevant past experience who is ready to pitch in and grow with us.
Our clients are developers, landowners, and businesses. They hire us to get things done and to be the subject matter experts, whether we are advocating in a hearing, writing a brief, drafting a development agreement, or lobbying for change. We handle rezonings, comprehensive plan amendments, Live Local Act projects, environmental permits, and conservation easements.
You'll work directly with our managing partner alongside our team of attorneys, land planners, and paralegals. You'll get your own matters, client interaction, and your own time at the podium early, with close mentoring along the way.
A successful attorney in this role will be open to working on a team even when the file isn't yours, telling a client news they may not want to hear, and remaining calm in the wake of long multi-hour public hearings.

Key Responsibilities

·     Entitlements:
Run rezonings, comprehensive plan amendments, variances, Live Local Act, and other entitlements applications from due diligence through the final hearing.
·     Hearings and Advocacy:
Present to hearing officers, planning commissions, city councils, and county commissions.
·     Environmental and Conservation:
Handle environmental resource permits, wetland and mitigation issues, brownfield designations, and conservation easement transactions.
·     Research and Writing:
Draft applications, memos, development agreements, and litigation and appellate briefs. Conduct legal research through statutes, case law, and public records.
·     Community and Political Engagement:
Engage with neighbors and the community about your projects, and develop and manage relationships with elected officials.
·     Team Collaboration:
Work with our planners and paralegals as peers. Pitch in where needed, including on matters that aren't yours, in a low-ego, high-support environment.
·     Client Relationship Management:
Demonstrate an "owner’s mentality" in client communications, managing relationships with a strong sense of accountability and responsiveness.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

·     Education & Licensure:
Juris Doctorate (J.D.) from an accredited law school and an active license to practice law in Florida.
·     Experience:
Minimum of 2 years in Florida land use, zoning, local government, or environmental law. We value diverse backgrounds and welcome candidates with non-traditional career paths.
·     Hearings:
Substantial experience in both written and oral advocacy presenting to a board, council, commission, hearing officer, or court.
·     Mindset:
A collaborative, "roll-up-your-sleeves" attitude. We operate as a tight-knit team where ego is left at the door.
·     Communication:
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; ability to translate complex legal concepts into actionable advice for clients.
·     Location:
Ability to work from our Tampa office in the 33606 area and to travel to hearings, site visits, and client meetings around Florida.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

·     Travel and evening hearings:
Ability to travel by car to hearings, site visits, and client meetings, and to lead evening public hearings that sometimes run late.
·     Stationary Work:
Ability to remain in a stationary position (sitting or standing) for extended periods (up to 75% of the workday) while performing computer and/or desk-based tasks.
·     Visual Acuity:
Ability to read and analyze data on a computer screen and in printed legal documents for long durations.
·     Communication:
Ability to clearly communicate information and ideas so others will understand; must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations via phone and in person.
·     Work Environment:
This is a professional office environment with a moderate noise level (telephones, printers, and foot traffic).

Preferred skills

·     Certifications:
Florida Bar board certification in City, County and Local Government Law, or AICP.
·     Local Experience:
Prior work with Tampa Bay local government staff is a significant plus.
·     Subject Matter:
Experience with the land use, development, Live Local Act, affordable housing, or environmental permitting.
·     Tech Savvy:
Proficiency with PracticePanther, Box, and Google Suite, and comfort working with AI tools such as Claude and Gemini.

WHY JOIN US?

·     Culture:
A "tight-knit" and collaborative environment where every team member’s contribution is recognized and mentoring is standard.
·     Health & Wellness:
Comprehensive medical and ancillary insurance coverage.
·     Financial Security:
Competitive pay, 401(k) retirement plan with company matching plus short-term and long-term disability insurance.
·     Work-Life Balance:
Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) and paid holidays.
·     No Book of Business Required:
We have a strong foundation of work; we just need your excellent counsel and client management.

Please send resume and writing sample to sbrooks@barbascremer.com. Use subject line: Land Use Attorney.

COMPANY DESCRIPTION

Barbas Cremer, PLLC, founded in 2017, is a law firm based in Florida that advises businesses, landowners, and developers. Known for its work in employment, business, land use, and environmental law, our team draws on firsthand experience in business operations, land planning, and policy development. Our portfolio includes major Tampa redevelopment projects and contributions to Florida legislative updates and U.S. Supreme Court decisions. Recognized by Chambers USA, Super Lawyers, and Best Lawyers in America, we pride ourselves on offering clients practical legal solutions rooted in real-world business understanding.

jobs.title: Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internships
jobs.description:
Internship
1200 Getty Center Drive, Los Angeles, CA 90049
Posted 5 days ago
$45,500 / Year

Website J. Paul Getty Trust

Summary

The Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internships aim to increase the number of students from underrepresented backgrounds preparing to enroll in graduate degree programs related to museum conservation.

An advanced degree is essential to a conservation career and few programs exist. Applicants often boost their credentials by completing prerequisite courses and undertaking up to thousands of hours of conservation training, usually unpaid. Graduate program administrators say these realities have limited opportunities for underrepresented groups.

Launched in 2020 as a pilot program, the Getty Post-Baccalaureate Internships are the first nationwide effort to provide yearlong financial support and hands-on conservation experience to underrepresented post-baccalaureates who are preparing to apply to conservation graduate programs.

Program Structure

Based on departmental needs, interns will be placed at conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center and Getty Villa in Los Angeles for the first six months of their internships, and then at a Los Angeles-area museum or within a different conservation department at Getty for the second six months of the internship. Areas of focus for the internship may include American Indian collections and artifacts, conservation science, antiquities, sculpture and decorative arts, works on paper, photographs, or books.

For the second six months of the internship, placements have been previously offered at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures; the Huntington; the Fowler Museum at UCLA; the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA); and the Autry Museum of the American West.

Key Details

Grant Amount:
$45,500, plus $1,500 towards relocation expenses to Los Angeles and an additional $4,000 towards educational reimbursements, certificate courses in conservation, domestic conservation conference attendance, or other professional-development opportunities related to the internship.

Duration:
12 months (September 7, 2027 — August 25, 2028)

Schedule:
FT

Deadline:
November 3, 2026

Eligibility

While these internships are intended for students from backgrounds underrepresented in the conservation field, Getty encourages eligible candidates from all backgrounds to apply for consideration. Getty is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any protected trait under the law. Candidates will have the opportunity to demonstrate their interest in museum conservation and how they might add new and underrepresented perspectives, which can include – among other things – socio-economic status, cultural background, physical or other disability, geographical origin, and/or any other life experiences.

Candidates Must

Be a United States citizen or permanent resident eligible to work in the United States (permanent residents are non-citizens authorized to live and work in the United States on a permanent basis, also known as “green card” holders). Those with DACA (Deferred Action for Childhood Arrival) status valid through the internship period are also eligible.
Be committed to a career in conservation and possess a strong desire to attend graduate school to further that goal.
Be able to demonstrate previous experience in conservation.

About

The Getty Conservation Institute serves professionals working to conserve the world’s cultural heritage through our scientific research, education and training, field projects, and sharing of our knowledge and expertise. Our work is driven by the values of excellence, innovation, leadership, collaboration, and service.
